clue.text: Argue fallaciously, or plead " Pop it !"?

definitions.meaning: to assume the very point under dispute is the logical fallacy called petitio principii
read literally, to plead that a suitor should at last ask for one's hand in marriage

explanation.walkthrough: To 'pop the question' is to propose marriage, so someone urging 'Pop it!' is literally asking for that proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the circular-reasoning fallacy, and read word by word it means pleading for a marriage proposal.

clue.text: A priest an admirer of Charles

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns out to be a fan of some Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia, so a devotee of them is an Elian; 'A' simply introduces the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his essays Elia, and a follower of that writer takes the adjective formed from the pen name.

parts.note: a jack of all trades has every craft at his fingertips, so he is a skilled worker covering the whole range

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the proverbial jack of all trades.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled craftsman follows a trade, and a jack of all trades follows all of them at once.

parts.note: because Pharaoh would not free the Israelites, the last plague in Exodus killed every Egyptian first-born child

explanation.definitionFit: The tenth plague struck the first-born, the oldest child of each Egyptian family.

clue.text: The first lady in a flashy suit

definitions.text: The first lady in a flashy suit

parts.words: The first lady in a flashy suit
parts.note: the leading female card in the suit of sparkling gems ranks first among its court cards after the king

explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife and 'flashy suit' clothing; the suit is a card suit named after gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Among playing cards the highest female figure of the jewelled suit is that suit's royal woman.

parts.note: King Lear on the heath is battered by wind, rain and thunder, which he addresses directly; such forces are also the basic constituents of matter

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play the storm-beaten king cries 'I tax not you, you elements, with unkindness'.
explanation.definitionFit: The weather that torments Lear is the classical forces of nature, and the same word means fundamentals.

clue.text: One for whom a fly waits at the terminus of the line

definitions.text: One for whom a fly waits at the terminus of the line

parts.words: One for whom a fly waits at the terminus of the line
parts.note: an angler's artificial fly sits at the end of the fishing line waiting for a river fish to bite

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cab (a 'fly' was a hired carriage) meeting a passenger at a railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish is the usual quarry of fly-fishing.

parts.note: government by a small group: the few rule, not the many

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' reads as 'usually'; here it means 'as rulers'.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of government is rule by a small privileged group.

clue.text: She kept up the spirits of the troops

definitions.text: She kept up the spirits of the troops

parts.words: She kept up the spirits of the troops
parts.note: a woman attached to a French regiment who sold food and liquor to the soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' means morale in the surface but liquor in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen-woman following French armies supplied the soldiers with drink, literally their spirits.

indicators.note: back says the letters of the short name and the zero are read from right to left

parts.note: Tim is the short form of the name Timothy; that the full name also starts with the same four letters is a coincidence, as Love supplies the O
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man called Timothy that Love wants him left out of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TIMO into the answer. 'Include me out' is a famous Sam Goldwyn mangling of 'leave me out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldwyn's phrase means to leave someone out, which is to exclude or skip.

parts.note: Robert Burns wrote the song 'John ..., my jo', and a demijohn is a big bottle that a drinking crony might share

explanation.walkthrough: Burns is the Scottish poet; 'demijohn' plays on John as half of a full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burns song names a John with this surname, the old companion of its singer.

parts.note: a gig is a light carriage, also called a trap, so 'into the carriage' gives the French en plus a trap; to put into a trap means to catch

explanation.walkthrough: Carlyle coined 'gigmanity' for the gig-owning respectable class; the gig is a trap, and 'en voiture' is French for 'all aboard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone is to catch them, literally to get them into a trap.

definitions.meaning: a small metric unit of mass
a pulse is an edible seed such as a pea or lentil, and chickpeas go by this name in India

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a metric unit of mass and the Indian name for the chickpea, a legume.

indicators.note: a mutation is a change, so the letters of the name Rose Viner are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A geneticist reports on an inherited change seen in someone called Rose Viner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutation of' rearranges ROSEVINER, and the whole clue describes the answer: a throwback to an ancestral type.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the term means a return to an ancestral type, an inherited change backward.

clue.text: In Pharaoh's dream they stood for years of plenty

definitions.text: In Pharaoh's dream they stood for years of plenty

parts.words: In Pharaoh's dream they stood for years of plenty
parts.note: Joseph read the seven well-fed cows of Pharaoh's dream as seven good harvests; animals fattened for market go by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Livestock fattened for slaughter matches the sleek cattle that Joseph interpreted as good years.

parts.note: the Inner Temple and Middle Temple are Inns of Court, and lawyers are called to the bar, which is also where drinks are served in an inn

explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court are London's barristers' societies; an inn also has a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: This former gateway in London stands by the Temple, home of two legal Inns, and its name pairs a church with a pub counter.

parts.note: medieval belief held that a kind of wild goose hatched from the shelled sea creatures that cling to ships

explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers an Arctic goose and the shelled crustacean once thought to grow into it.

parts.note: in du Maurier's novel the hypnotist controls Trilby, a singer, and a trilby is also a soft felt hat

explanation.walkthrough: A trilby is a felt hat named after du Maurier's heroine, who sings only under hypnosis.
explanation.definitionFit: The hypnotist in the novel Trilby rules the heroine, so he is her controlling master.

parts.note: hawthorn blossom is called may, and the rhyme 'Here we go gathering nuts in May' was said to mean knots (posies) of it

explanation.walkthrough: The children's song 'Here we go gathering nuts in May' puts the month next to nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn flowers go by the month's name, and the plural fits sprays of that blossom.

clue.text: Make one beloved — a ring may do so

definitions.text: Make one beloved — a ring may do so

parts.words: Make one beloved — a ring may do so
parts.note: to win affection; and a ring at the end of the ear lobe, an earring, is also a way to charm

explanation.walkthrough: The ring suggested is an engagement ring, which wins a partner's affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection is to make them hold you dear.

indicators.note: surrounded says the firm's short form is placed inside the gun's name

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun

explanation.surface: A firm finds itself encircled by gunmen somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun-surrounded' reads as a bloodthirsty scene, but the hyphen hides a container signal. Brecon is a Welsh market town below the Brecon Beacons.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town lies in mid-Wales, below the mountain range named after it.

clue.text: Port can be something of a tonic or fuddling

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A glass of port, the clue says, can be part tonic and part befuddlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the drink; it is a harbour, the Greek island's main town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island's capital is a harbour city, so a ship could dock there.

parts.note: Mona is a woman's name
Lisa is another woman's name

explanation.surface: A pair of ladies grin together in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: Two girls' names joined make Leonardo's portrait, famous for its enigmatic smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait is the world's best-known painted smile.

parts.note: fathers who beget a family line, as stallions are named in a horse's pedigree

explanation.definitionFit: Male parents, especially of thoroughbreds, beget the line of descent.

clue.text: Bird under the wheel turns unreliable.

indicators.note: a bird crushed under a turning wheel is rolled over, so its name is read backwards

parts.note: a rail is a marsh bird such as the water rail

explanation.surface: A bird run over by a cart becomes an unpredictable thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the wheel turns' reverses RAIL. The definition stands for an unreliable person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths cannot be trusted, an unreliable person.

definitions.meaning: a low stand with partitions for holding sheet music or papers
a see is a bishop's seat or diocese, here the senior English archbishopric

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a music-stand cabinet and the Kent cathedral city that is England's chief archbishopric.

clue.text: You'll be safe if you deal with them

definitions.text: You'll be safe if you deal with them

parts.words: You'll be safe if you deal with them
parts.note: firms that sell policies make you financially secure against loss

explanation.definitionFit: Companies selling cover against loss make clients secure.

clue.text: An academy holiday is most infrequent

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
a holiday is a rest from work

explanation.surface: Breaks at an art school, it seems, happen hardly ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy is London's art institution, abbreviated RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of an adjective meaning seldom seen or happening.
